Guides

Choosing ingredients

Variety, including bitter greens, matters more than an organic label. A short list of foods is genuinely unsuitable.

Findings

Offer bitter and savoury flavours early. Babies who meet green vegetables in the first weeks of solids are more willing to eat them later.
Put an iron food on the early shopping list. Meat, lentils, beans, tofu, and fortified infant cereal are the practical sources.
A short avoid-list is enough. Honey, added salt, added sugar, rice drinks, whole nuts, unpasteurised dairy, and a few fish are the items with a real reason behind them.

Variety, including the awkward tastes

ESPGHAN asks for a range of flavours and textures, bitter greens included. A month of only sweet pear and banana teaches a narrow palate. Broccoli, spinach in a mixture, bean, and fish can appear in the first fortnight.

Organic produce has not been shown to change allergy or growth outcomes for infants. Wash it. Peel when the skin is tough or heavily soiled. Seasonality is a pleasure and a budget tool, not a safety rule.

Build around iron

A useful kitchen keeps one iron food ready: cooked mince in the freezer, red lentils in the cupboard, unsalted beans, eggs, or a fortified cereal you actually tolerate the taste of. Pair plant iron with fruit or pepper for vitamin C.

Rice cereal is optional. It is not required for sleep or for a first spoon, and rice drinks are a different product entirely. Children under five should not drink rice drinks, because of arsenic.

Foods with a specific reason to skip or change

Honey, even baked, can contain spores that produce infant botulism. It waits until after the first birthday, and it is still sugar then. Salt waits too: an infant’s daily ceiling is under 1 gram, which is already reached by ordinary foods, so none is added and stock cubes, ham, and soy sauce stay out. Sugar and fruit juice are not needed; whole fruit is the right form.

Whole nuts, whole grapes, popcorn, and hard dried fruit are choking hazards. Shark, swordfish, and marlin are too high in mercury. Unpasteurised milk and mould-ripened cheeses can carry listeria. Undercooked kidney beans and other dried beans can cause rapid illness; boil them until they are completely soft. Liver is nutritious and so high in vitamin A that once a week, in a small portion, is the ceiling.
